1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6.name: English Defence
1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6.background: The Leicester player P. N. Wallis investigated the opening in the late 1940s and early 1950s, and in the 1970s it was taken up by leading English players such as Tony Miles and Raymond Keene. Viktor Korchnoi used it successfully in game 6 of his Candidates semi-final match against Lev Polugaevsky at Évian in 1977.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.e4.strategy: Takes the broad pawn centre at once, which is exactly what the English Defence invites. Black plans to undermine it from a distance, starting with the bishop on b7 hitting e4, so White gains space but has to keep the centre pawns protected.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.Nc3.strategy: Develops a piece and controls e4, so Black's fianchettoed bishop meets resistance on the long diagonal. White gives up the immediate broad pawn centre for a flexible set-up in which Black can pin the knight and the fight turns on who controls e4.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.Nf3.strategy: Develops the knight and covers e5 and d4 while committing nothing: White can still build a broad pawn centre later or settle for a flexible set-up. The price is that it claims no space yet, so Black develops the bishop on the long diagonal at leisure.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.d5.strategy: Gains space and hits e6 at once, but the pawn then stands on the very diagonal Black's bishop will attack from b7. White gets a cramping pawn and a closed game; Black has easy targets for the queen and bishop and no trouble equalising.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.e4 Bb7.strategy: The idea of the opening: the bishop attacks the e4 pawn at once and eyes the long diagonal. White defends with a developing move and keeps a small edge, so the bishop alone does not undermine the broad centre and needs help from other pieces.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.e4 Bb4+.strategy: Develops with check and undermines the broad centre from the side instead of occupying it. If White blocks with the knight, the pin ties it to the king and e4 comes under pressure once the other bishop reaches b7; after a trade of bishops Black reaches an equal game.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.e4 Qh4.strategy: Hits the undefended e4 pawn at once, but the queen is out alone. White defends with a developing move, and Nf3 then attacks the queen with tempo, so Black loses time and White keeps the broad centre.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.e4 Bb7 4.Bd3.strategy: The most natural defence: it protects e4 and develops a piece towards the kingside without weakening the pawns around the king. The price is that the bishop blocks the queen's view of d4, which Black can attack at once.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.e4 Bb7 4.f3.strategy: Props up e4 with a pawn, which keeps the pieces free and the centre intact. But it takes the f3 square from the knight and opens the e1-h4 diagonal, so ...Qh4+ forces a loosening g3.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.e4 Bb7 4.Nc3.strategy: A natural developing move that guards e4 and prepares to complete the centre. It can be pinned at once, though: with the knight tied to the king, e4 is defended only on paper, so White must spend a move shoring the pawn up again.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.e4 Bb7 4.Qc2.strategy: Protects e4 along the diagonal without blocking a piece or weakening a pawn. The queen is committed early, though: a queen sortie to h4 hits e4 a second time, and White must bring another defender at once.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.e4 Bb7 4.Bd3 Nc6.name: English Defence: Perrin Variation
1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.e4 Bb7 4.Bd3 Nc6.strategy: Hits the d4 pawn, which the bishop has left without the queen's protection. Black also prepares to trade the knight for the bishop that guards e4, and so to weaken White's hold on the centre.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.e4 Bb7 4.Bd3 Bb4+.strategy: Develops with a check and prepares to hit e4 a second time with a pawn. If the knight blocks it is pinned, so the bishop on d3 and the pawn on e4 are less secure than they look, and Black gets active piece play against White's broad centre.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.e4 Bb7 4.Bd3 Nf6.strategy: Hits e4 a second time and develops, so White has to add a defender at once. The obvious 5.e5 kicks the knight, but it opens the long diagonal to the g2 pawn, which has no defender once the bishop has left f1.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.e4 Bb7 4.f3 f5.strategy: Challenges the e4 pawn right away, but with f3 behind it White can take on f5 and Black's kingside is the one that is left open. A thematic strike that needs more preparation to be sound.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.e4 Bb7 4.f3 Bb4+.strategy: Develops with check and points the bishop at the defenders of e4. If the knight blocks it is pinned and Black can undermine the centre from the flank; if White trades bishops, it gives up its dark-squared bishop with the king's side already loosened by f3.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.e4 Bb7 4.f3 Qh4+.strategy: Checks at once and forces g3 or a king move, since f3 has opened the diagonal to the king. White's kingside is loosened for good, but the queen is offside after the check and the check costs Black a developing tempo.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.e4 Bb7 4.f3 f5 5.exf5.strategy: Opens the centre by taking the pawn. The pawn on f3 keeps the bishop's long diagonal shut, but it leaves the e1-h4 diagonal open, so White has to be ready to answer ...Qh4+ with g3.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.e4 Bb7 4.f3 f5 5.Nc3.strategy: Gives e4 a second defender and develops, keeping the tension instead of resolving it. The centre pawns stay intact, but a pin on the knight leaves e4 held only once again, so White has to resolve the tension with care.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.e4 Bb7 4.f3 f5 5.e5.strategy: Shuts the centre, takes e5 from Black and fixes the e6 pawn, so Black has no capture on e4 to open the game. But the f3 pawn remains a weakness: the diagonal to the king is still open and the bishop on b7 bears on f3.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.e4 Bb7 4.f3 f5 5.exf5.name: English Defence: Poli Gambit
1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.e4 Bb7 4.f3 f5 5.exf5.strategy: Hits f5 a second time and offers the e6-pawn for quick play. If White takes it, the rim knight reaches f5 with tempo and Black regains the pawn with active pieces. A gambit that asks Black to know the lines, but it gives Black a level game.

Wins the pawn back at once and keeps the structure healthy, but opens the e-file towards Black's own king. White develops with tempo and has Qe2+ in hand, so Black stays under pressure. Sound, but White keeps the initiative.

Develops while leaving the pawn on f5 alone, a gambit that White can accept by taking on e6 or holding f5. The extra pawn stays with White, and the knight also blocks the queen's route to h4, so the check that f3 invited is gone.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.Nc3 Bb7.strategy: Puts the bishop on the long diagonal at once, where it eyes e4 and the whole centre from a distance. Black lets White build a pawn centre and prepares to attack it, and keeps the pin of the knight in reserve.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.Nc3 d5.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Alapin Variation
1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.Nc3 d5.strategy: Takes the centre directly with a classical, solid set-up. But the pawn on d5 is pressed at once by White's c-pawn and knight, and it blocks the diagonal the b6 plan wants for the bishop. Sound, if less ambitious than undermining the centre from afar.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.Nc3 Bb4.strategy: Pins the knight to the king at once, so White must spend time breaking the pin, and Black can take on c3 to double White's pawns when it suits. The cost is a delay in developing the queen's bishop.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.Nc3 Bb7 4.e4.strategy: Builds the broad pawn centre with the knight already out to guard e4, the set-up the English Defence invites. White gets space and a free hand in the middlegame, but the centre pawns become targets for the bishop on b7 and the pawn thrust ...f5.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.Nc3 Bb7 4.Nf3.strategy: Develops the knight and covers e5 and d4 before deciding on the pawn centre. White asks Black to commit first and accepts that a pin on c3 is part of the game; the broad centre with e4 remains available later.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.Nc3 Bb7 4.e3.strategy: Quiet and solid: the pawn guards d4 and opens the way for the king's bishop, but White gives up the broad centre that e4 would build and lets Black pin the knight on c3 at once. A sound set-up that asks little of Black.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.Nc3 Bb7 4.e4 f5.strategy: Attacks e4 a second time, but 5.e5 answers at once: White gains space, takes f6 from the g8-knight and leaves e6 and the e8-h5 diagonal weak.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.Nc3 Bb7 4.e4 Bb4.strategy: Pins the knight that holds e4, so the pawn the bishop on b7 attacks is guarded only on paper and White has to spend a move shoring it up. Black undermines the broad centre from the side and keeps the option of trading on c3.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.Nc3 Bb7 4.e4 Nf6.strategy: Attacks e4 a second time, but White simply defends it with a developing move such as Bd3 and keeps the broad centre. Unlike ...Bb4, the knight does not pin the c3 knight, so e4 is never in danger and Black has found no way to undermine the centre.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.Nc3 Bb7 4.e4 f5 5.exf5.strategy: Takes the pawn and opens the centre. The bishop's diagonal now runs right up to g2, which the bishop on f1 guards, and White keeps its pawns on d4 and c4. If Black does not recapture, White stays a pawn up.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.Nc3 Bb7 4.e4 f5 5.d5.name: English Defence: Hartlaub Gambit Declined
1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.Nc3 Bb7 4.e4 f5 5.d5.strategy: Presses on e6 but gives up the e4 pawn: after 5...fxe4 White gets space and little else for it, and the position is level. White throws away the lead that the stronger pawn advance keeps.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.Nc3 Bb7 4.e4 f5 5.Bd3.strategy: Defends e4 with a developing move, but 5...Bb4 pins the c3 knight that also guards e4. The pawn is attacked twice and defended once, so White must find a way to hold it, and Black equalises.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.Nc3 Bb7 4.e4 f5 5.e5.strategy: Pushes past the attack: e4 no longer needs defending, White gains space and takes f6 from the g8-knight. The e6-pawn and the e8-h5 diagonal are weak, since Qh5+ is a check. Black gets the long diagonal for the bishop, but White keeps the lasting edge.

1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.Nc3 Bb7 4.e4 f5 5.exf5.name: English Defence: Hartlaub Gambit Accepted
1.d4 e6 2.c4 b6 3.Nc3 Bb7 4.e4 f5 5.exf5.strategy: Develops and keeps the queen check off by covering h5, but leaves the f5 pawn alone. White takes on e6 or develops and keeps the extra pawn, and the knight does not win it back, so Black has little to show for it.

Recaptures with the e-pawn and restores material equality, opening the e-file and keeping the pawn's control of e4. White's queen can give a check, but Black meets it and keeps a sound position, slightly loosened on the kingside.
Pins the knight but ignores the pawn on f5: White can take on e6, where the pawn attacks d7, and Black ends up a pawn down for little more than a possible doubled pawn on c3.
